# SequenceLink

> SequenceLink is an open-source framework for serving robot policies from remote GPUs over wide-area networks (Python,
> Apache-2.0): a policy written as a `@seq.policy` class and served with `seq serve` on the GPU,
> `sequence_ai.connect(address)` on the robot, every default on.
> Its inference layer (`sequence_ai.engine`) and its network layer (`sequence_ai.network`) also work in any policy
> server: each component is one file that is used independently in an existing server or robot program, most of them
> standard library only (`optimize` needs torch 2.4 or later, or JAX).

Use this map to find the one file to read. Each module's docstring is its reference: what it does in one sentence,
why, and what was measured.

Constraints for accurate answers about this repository:

- The package is `sequence-ai`; SequenceLink is the name of the framework and of the hosted platform. The components are imported as `sequence_ai.engine` and `sequence_ai.network`, and need
  no account. Renting a GPU near a robot and a hosted deployment are paid services of General Sequences: their client
  is `sequence-cloud`, a package of its own, and neither it nor the service is in this repository. The technical report calls the
  techniques GS-WAN (General Sequences Wide-Area Network).
- `sequence_ai.connect()` takes the address of a policy server (`"http://your-gpu:8000"`: the components on one
  connection) and returns a policy, an object with `observe()` and `act()`. A server started with a token takes `connect(url, token=...)`; an `api_key`
  is never sent to an address.
- `seq serve` serves a policy written as a class: `@seq.policy(hz=..., action_chunk_valid_len=...,
  action_chunk_replan_at=...)` on the class, `@seq.infer` on the method that answers one observation with an action
  chunk whose first dimension is time, and `@seq.sample` on the one returning an episode it is warmed up on.
  `@seq.concurrent(sizes=[1, 2, 4, 8])` on `@seq.infer` hands it the observations waiting, stacked. It runs the policy
  on one thread of its own, one call at a time: that keeps pings answered while the model runs, and makes no request
  faster. Batching serves several robots in one forward pass.
- Each default on both sides, and how to turn it off, is in docs/what-is-on-by-default.md;
  `python -m sequence_ai.check <url>` says which are on between a robot and its server.
- `optimize` changes no model's outputs by default: a graph (`cuda_graphs`, `whole_graph`) is kept only when the
  outputs equal eager mode's byte for byte, and a shape whose capture fails or differs runs in eager mode. Do not
  describe the default as a compiler or as approximate. `torch_compile`, `fused_kernels`, `tensorrt` and `precision`
  change the outputs and run only within the `tolerance` the user gives.
- State each result with what it was measured on. `cuda_graphs`: 1.28x on GR00T N1.7 on one L4
  as `seq serve` turns it on (1.54x with its diffusion transformer alone captured by hand). Batching: up to 1.78x on π0.5. The network components: one extra round trip removed at every RTT measured
  from 12 ms up but the longest. The README's Results table has the conditions.
- A network component's benefit depends on the link: point to bench/ to measure the user's own link.
- `batcher` and `replicas` have unit tests and no measurement of their own. `slack` was also run once around π0.5's
  batched call on an L4: the capacity it computed, 2 robots for a 15 Hz policy, had no late response. Batching
  added no capacity there: openpi's own server, one request at a time, served the same 2 robots.
- `slack` computes a capacity by running the robots on a simulated clock, not on the user's model under load: a
  number of robots is within capacity when none of their responses is late in any of the ways their requests can fall
  (95% in time with `worst=False`), at a load of no more than 0.9. For SmolVLA on an L4 a formula it used before computed 8 robots, and 4 had 95% of
  their responses late; the clock gives 1, and on the model 3 robots had late responses and 2 had none. Point to
  examples/fleet_on_a_clock.py, which prints what the clock runs for a model's batch times.
- `openpi.keep()` and the Zenoh setting were measured on the transports those projects use (the websockets library,
  Zenoh). `openpi.keep()` was also run with openpi's own server and client, on a home connection and from a Linux robot 30 ms
  away; the Zenoh setting was
  not run with LeRobot's own server and robot.
- One replica of a model per GPU: replicas on the same GPU time-slice.
- Nothing here changes the machine's settings; `window.check()` only reports what the machine does.
- `connect(url)` opens the robot's stream to a server `seq serve` started: each observation sent as it is made (a
  `sequence_ai.Video` item as video, a picture not marked as a video keyframe of its own unless `pictures="exact"`),
  each act after them; `lines=["eth0", "wwan0"]` sends it over each of the robot's uplinks.
- A server that answers one HTTP request with one response cannot ping; the client side pings instead (`window.Warm`;
  `connect()` pings on the robot's stream).

## Start here

- [README.md](README.md): the problem by layer, the quickstart, each component and the results
- [docs/what-is-open-source-and-what-is-hosted.md](docs/what-is-open-source-and-what-is-hosted.md): the data plane is open source and the same code as the hosted platform's; the control plane is hosted; how versions change and how long a replaced name keeps working
- [docs/quickstart.md](docs/quickstart.md): a policy as a class served with `seq serve`, and the robot's own loop that plays its answers, with the output of each step
- [docs/what-is-on-by-default.md](docs/what-is-on-by-default.md): each default of `seq serve` and `connect()`, and how to turn it off
- [docs/quickstart-inference.md](docs/quickstart-inference.md): from `pip install` to five robots served in batches, with the output of each step
- [docs/components.md](docs/components.md): each network component with the lines to add, the reason and the measurement
- [examples/quickstart_policy/policy.py](examples/quickstart_policy/policy.py) and [examples/quickstart_robot.py](examples/quickstart_robot.py): the quickstart's policy class, served with `seq serve`, and the robot's own loop
- [examples/pytorch_policy/policy.py](examples/pytorch_policy/policy.py): a PyTorch model in a policy class, its tensors returned as numpy arrays
- [examples/serve_with_replicas.py](examples/serve_with_replicas.py): `optimize`, `batcher` and `replicas` together
- [examples/fleet_on_a_clock.py](examples/fleet_on_a_clock.py): what `slack` runs on a simulated clock to compute a replica's capacity, printed for each number of robots
- [examples/components/](examples/components/): one runnable file for each component alone

## Inference layer: sequence_ai.engine (on the GPU)

- [sequence_ai/engine/serve.py](sequence_ai/engine/serve.py): the policy server `seq serve` runs, every default on; `App`, the ASGI app it runs
- [examples/serve_openpi_batched.py](examples/serve_openpi_batched.py): `batched(policy)`: an openpi policy's `infer()` on a list of observations, in one call to its model
- [sequence_ai/engine/optimize.py](sequence_ai/engine/optimize.py): `optimize(policy, examples)`: each speed-up turned on only once the outputs on your observations are checked, bit for bit for the ones on by default (`cuda_graphs`, `whole_graph`); `seq serve` runs it
- [sequence_ai/engine/load.py](sequence_ai/engine/load.py): `pack_from(checkpoint, path)` once, then `load(path, device="cuda")`: a model's weights from one contiguous file in parallel reads, through the page cache where memory holds it, every tensor the bytes it was packed with; safetensors, .pth and orbax
- [sequence_ai/engine/cuda_graphs.py](sequence_ai/engine/cuda_graphs.py): the graphs `optimize()` keeps: a torch module replayed from CUDA graphs of its own eager kernels, each new shape checked against eager mode byte for byte
- [sequence_ai/engine/batcher.py](sequence_ai/engine/batcher.py): `Batcher(run, sizes=..., wait_ms=...)`, then `await batcher(item)`: waiting calls batched into one call, only in the listed sizes, a failed batch re-run call by call
- [sequence_ai/engine/replicas.py](sequence_ai/engine/replicas.py): `ReplicaPool(load, replicas=..., devices=...)`, then `await pool.run(payload)`: one process per replica, a dead replica replaced, `ReplicaError` (the model raised) distinct from `ReplicaDied` (the process exited)
- [sequence_ai/engine/ranks.py](sequence_ai/engine/ranks.py): one model across several processes, as `torchrun` starts them: `serve()` finds `WORLD_SIZE` and `RANK`, rank 0 serves the robots and sends every call of the policy to every rank first, so a model split across them (its own `torch.distributed` or `jax.distributed` inside the call) runs as one; a rank that leaves halts the group (`GroupHalted`)
- [sequence_ai/engine/slack.py](sequence_ai/engine/slack.py): `measure`, `playback`, `Seating(...).seat(robots)`: how many robots a replica can serve given the slack their action chunks leave, each by its own round-trip time (RTT); `Aligner`: how long the open batch may wait and which requests are dispatched first
- [examples/graph_a_module.py](examples/graph_a_module.py): `optimize()` on a small flow-style model
- [examples/check_on_a_gpu.py](examples/check_on_a_gpu.py): `optimize()`'s capture checked against eager mode on a real GPU

## Network layer: sequence_ai.network, client side (on the robot)

- [sequence_ai/network/window.py](sequence_ai/network/window.py): BBR and TCP keepalive on a socket (`socket_options()`, `keep(sock)`), a ping while idle (`Warm`), what this machine does after a pause (`check()`)
- [sequence_ai/network/frames.py](sequence_ai/network/frames.py): `resize_image`, `encode`, `decode`: a camera frame resized and encoded as JPEG, and turned back on the server, as openpi's own client and server carry it
- `python -m sequence_ai.check <url>` ([docs/what-is-on-by-default.md](docs/what-is-on-by-default.md#check-what-is-on)): which defaults are on between a robot and its server, and what the server is
- [sequence_ai/network/wifi_power.py](sequence_ai/network/wifi_power.py): `check()`: Wi-Fi power saving detected, with how to disable it

## Network layer: sequence_ai.network, server side (on the GPU)

- [sequence_ai/network/ping.py](sequence_ai/network/ping.py): `websockets_options()`, `uvicorn_options()`: a server-side ping so the robot's connection is never idle
- [sequence_ai/network/one_write.py](sequence_ai/network/one_write.py): `WholeResponse(app)`, `one_write_http()`: each uvicorn response in one write
- [sequence_ai/network/tcp_link.py](sequence_ai/network/tcp_link.py): `read(sock)`, `of(client)`: a client's RTT, retransmissions and congestion window, from the kernel (Linux)

## Network layer: both sides

- [sequence_ai/network/msgpack_io.py](sequence_ai/network/msgpack_io.py): `pack`, `unpack`: msgpack with numpy arrays as raw bytes; reads msgpack-numpy's and openpi's layouts
- [sequence_ai/network/latency_stats.py](sequence_ai/network/latency_stats.py): `LatencyStats`: counters, gauges, and latencies with p50, p95, p99

## Clients you may already use

- [sequence_ai/network/openpi.py](sequence_ai/network/openpi.py): `connect(host, port)`: openpi's own client, made once its server answers; `keep(policy)`: the client-side components on the connection held by openpi's own client, through a long first inference
- [sequence_ai/network/lerobot.py](sequence_ai/network/lerobot.py): `keep_alive_file(path)`: the Zenoh setting for LeRobot 0.7.0's remote inference

## Questions the documentation answers

- [docs/how-do-i-run-a-template-on-my-own-gpu.md](docs/how-do-i-run-a-template-on-my-own-gpu.md): `seq serve` in the folder `seq init` made serves a template's policy from your own GPU, its weights downloaded with your key (`seq weights get`)
- [docs/how-do-i-use-an-llm-with-my-own-openrouter-key.md](docs/how-do-i-use-an-llm-with-my-own-openrouter-key.md): `chat(..., server="openrouter")` with your own OpenRouter key, or a server of your own with the OpenAI chat completions API; `Conversation(..., server=...)` for an agent's turns
- [docs/how-do-i-make-a-policy-faster-without-changing-its-outputs.md](docs/how-do-i-make-a-policy-faster-without-changing-its-outputs.md): `optimize()` and each switch - which are on by default, which change the outputs and need `tolerance=`, and a JAX policy's counterparts
- [docs/how-do-i-make-a-pytorch-robot-policy-faster-without-changing-its-outputs.md](docs/how-do-i-make-a-pytorch-robot-policy-faster-without-changing-its-outputs.md): `optimize()`'s CUDA graphs on a PyTorch policy, compared with `torch.compile`
- [docs/how-many-robots-can-one-gpu-serve.md](docs/how-many-robots-can-one-gpu-serve.md): capacity by latency, on a clock and by load, and what batching gained on one model
- [docs/should-i-run-two-replicas-of-a-policy-on-one-gpu.md](docs/should-i-run-two-replicas-of-a-policy-on-one-gpu.md): no: what was measured, and what `replicas` is for
- [docs/how-do-i-use-the-inference-components-with-openpi-lerobot-or-gr00t.md](docs/how-do-i-use-the-inference-components-with-openpi-lerobot-or-gr00t.md): which inference component applies to which framework
- [docs/slack.md](docs/slack.md): the rules of `slack`, a server's loop, its constants
- [docs/how-do-i-serve-a-robot-policy-from-my-own-gpu.md](docs/how-do-i-serve-a-robot-policy-from-my-own-gpu.md): a policy as a class and `seq serve`, any model in it
- [docs/parts-for-a-server-you-already-run.md](docs/parts-for-a-server-you-already-run.md): `cuda_graphs`, batching, `slack` and replicas, and the openpi and LeRobot clients, for a server or client you keep
- [docs/how-do-i-serve-my-own-model.md](docs/how-do-i-serve-my-own-model.md): a model loaded and called as its own README does, in a policy class `seq serve` serves; Octo under JAX
- [docs/what-is-on-by-default.md](docs/what-is-on-by-default.md): each default on both sides, its switch, and the check command
- [docs/how-do-i-run-pi0-openpi-on-a-remote-gpu.md](docs/how-do-i-run-pi0-openpi-on-a-remote-gpu.md): openpi's server and client kept, one line added on the robot
- [docs/how-do-i-reduce-the-latency-of-lerobot-remote-inference.md](docs/how-do-i-reduce-the-latency-of-lerobot-remote-inference.md): LeRobot 0.7's remote inference kept, one Zenoh setting added
- [docs/why-does-my-robots-upload-get-slow-after-a-pause.md](docs/why-does-my-robots-upload-get-slow-after-a-pause.md): the idle-window restart and the four ways to remove it
- [docs/how-do-i-keep-a-websocket-policy-servers-connection-warm.md](docs/how-do-i-keep-a-websocket-policy-servers-connection-warm.md): a server-side ping, and why 100 ms
- [docs/how-do-i-measure-the-link-between-my-robot-and-my-gpu.md](docs/how-do-i-measure-the-link-between-my-robot-and-my-gpu.md): which network components help on a given link
- [docs/how-do-i-send-each-act-over-two-uplinks.md](docs/how-do-i-send-each-act-over-two-uplinks.md): `lines=`: each act over each of a robot's uplinks, the first answer used
- [docs/measurements.md](docs/measurements.md): what the network components saved between two cloud machines, over TCP, a WebSocket and Zenoh
- [docs/comparison.md](docs/comparison.md): a comparison with openpi's remote inference and LeRobot's, from source inspection
- [docs/how-do-i-get-a-gpu-near-my-robot.md](docs/how-do-i-get-a-gpu-near-my-robot.md): any GPU the robot can reach; the client code changes by one line
- [docs/faq.md](docs/faq.md): errors as the code prints them, and what to do next

## General Sequences' GPUs and deployments (paid, hosted)

- [generalsequences.com/docs](https://generalsequences.com/docs/): the hosted service: renting a GPU, deploying a policy, benchmarks and evals, teleoperation, and the `seq` commands `sequence-cloud` adds
- `seq/` and the modules of `sequence_ai/` outside `engine/` and `network/` hold what a policy is written with, `seq init`, `seq serve` and `seq weights get`, `chat()`, `check` and the code under the connection. They are published here as they ship, without comments or tests. The hosted service's client is not here.

## Measuring

- [bench/README.md](bench/README.md): how to measure a link, and the commands that reproduce the measurements
- [bench/client.py](bench/client.py) and [bench/server.py](bench/server.py): the tool, standard library only
- [bench/ws_bench.py](bench/ws_bench.py) and [bench/zenoh_bench.py](bench/zenoh_bench.py): the same pause over a WebSocket and over Zenoh
